## Context / Problem

The Gerrit instance role's Bedrock grant admits two Anthropic Claude model ARNs and nothing else. `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` (26 lines) carries one inline policy statement, sid `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly` (`:10`), with actions at `:11-14` and the two model ARNs at `:16-17`, attached as `aws_iam_role_policy.bedrock_converse` (`:22-26`).

Epic 62dc's similar-ticket retrieval configures `bedrock:amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` as its default embedding model — the model ADR 0122 measured. That ARN is outside the current grant, so the configured default is denied in this deployment. `evals/similar-tickets/README.md:131` records that the instance role is not Titan-capable; the benchmark was produced with separate credentials.

**This does not gate the feature.** Similar-ticket retrieval ships with a lexical tier that needs no provider and no credentials, and its embedding tier dispatches over pydantic-ai's provider-agnostic embeddings seam, so any installation can configure a different embedding model or run lexical-only. What this ticket fixes is narrower and local: making this deployment's *configured default* actually work, so the measured 0.876 semantic recall@5 is what runs here rather than the 0.823 lexical baseline.

The grant is also mis-scoped for the sid it carries. `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly` describes a vendor restriction that is not a requirement — the role may invoke whichever models rebar's operations need. The sid is a stale description of the current contents, not a constraint to preserve.

## Approach

Widen the existing statement rather than add a second one. One statement listing the models this role may invoke is the honest shape; a second statement would imply a scoping boundary that does not exist.

- Add the Titan embedding model ARN to the resource list at `:16-17`.
- Rename the sid from `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly` to one that describes the grant as it is, since the existing name asserts a vendor restriction that was never a requirement and is now false.
- Correct the header comment at `:4-6`, which describes the statement in the same Claude-only terms.
- Update `infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md`, which reproduces the sid verbatim at `:130` and `:239` for a separate external-CI OIDC role and claims at `:145` that it is `iam_s7.tf`'s shape "verbatim". Renaming the sid without touching the runbook makes that claim false.

The actions list at `:11-14` already contains `bedrock:InvokeModel`, which is what an embedding call authorizes against, so no action is added.

**No HCL-shape test is added, deliberately.** ADR 0059 (`docs/adr/0059-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md:294-312`) records that nothing verifies this file was applied before a change lands — tracked as bug `1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38` — and instructs that any IAM claim in the tree be read as "declared", not "live". A test asserting the HCL contains the ARN would pass against an unapplied plan and manufacture exactly the false confidence that bug describes. The only evidence that settles this is a real call, which is why the attestation below is the acceptance criterion.

A policy simulator cannot substitute for that call. ADR 0059 records that `bedrock:Converse` was once granted on simulator evidence and a real call disproved it, because Converse authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel`: the simulator answers what the policy language permits for the action you named, not which action the service actually checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` lists the Titan embedding model ARN in the `bedrock_converse` policy statement's resources, the statement's sid no longer asserts a vendor restriction, and the header comment at `:4-6` describes the statement's actual contents. Checked by: reading the file.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md` reproduces the current sid at every occurrence, and its claim that the policy matches `iam_s7.tf` verbatim is true after the rename. Checked by: grepping the old sid across `infra/` and finding no occurrence that refers to this role's statement.
- [ ] `[non-codebase]` An operator has applied the plan and recorded an attestation on this ticket that a real embedding call against `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` from the Gerrit instance role succeeded. The attestation states the change number and revision SHA applied, the UTC timestamp, the vector dimension count returned, and the operator identity. A policy-simulator result does not satisfy this. Checked by: the comment's presence on this ticket.
